meta.title: Operation of DSC/TGA Thermal Analyzer in Central Instrumentation Laboratory

sections.purpose: To characterize the thermal behaviour of pharmaceutical compounds and drug-excipient mixtures by measuring heat flow (DSC) and mass change (TGA) as a function of temperature, for polymorphism studies, compatibility testing, and purity determination.
sections.scope: Applicable to Central Instrumentation Laboratory for thermal characterization of pharmaceutical substances, excipients, and formulations for preformulation studies and stability profiling.
procedure: Switch on the DSC/TGA instrument and the associated cooling system (liquid nitrogen or Peltier cooling); allow 30–60 minutes warm-up.
Purge the furnace with dry nitrogen gas (20–50 mL/min) to provide an inert atmosphere and remove moisture.
For DSC: weigh 2–10 mg of the sample on a microbalance accurate to 0.01 mg; record the exact weight.
Place the sample in an aluminum DSC pan; seal using the encapsulating press (hermetically sealed for volatile samples; crimped/pierced for non-volatile).
Weigh an empty reference pan of the same type and lot.
Place the sample and reference pans on the DSC cell; close the furnace lid.
For TGA: weigh 5–20 mg of sample; place in the TGA platinum pan on the balance arm; close the furnace.

Program the temperature scan in the software: starting temperature (typically 25°C), heating rate (10°C/min standard; 5°C/min for higher resolution), end temperature (as per expected range, typically up to 300–400°C).
Start the run from the software — system will record the thermal events automatically.
After the run, allow the furnace to cool to room temperature under nitrogen purge.
Analyze the thermogram: DSC — identify Tg (glass transition), Tm (melting peak, onset temperature), ΔH (enthalpy); TGA — identify mass loss steps, onset temperatures, and residue.
Export the thermogram data and annotate all thermal events.
Record sample name, batch, exact weight, temperature program, and analysis results in the register.
precautions: Always purge with dry nitrogen — oxygen causes oxidative decomposition of pharmaceutical compounds above 200°C.
Weigh the sample accurately — DSC results are weight-normalized; weighing error directly affects enthalpy values.
Use appropriate pan type: open pans for volatile-containing samples (allow vapour escape); sealed pans for pressure-sensitive measurement.
Do not heat above the rated furnace temperature — overheating permanently damages the DSC sensor.
Allow full cool-down under nitrogen before opening the furnace — thermal shock damages the sensor.
For explosive or peroxide-forming materials, consult the safety officer before running DSC — sealed pans can rupture.
Calibrate the DSC annually using certified melting point standards (indium, zinc, lead).
